issues.legal_issue: An appellate order confirming a land-ceiling determination is subject to revision by a higher authority even when the governing scheme describes the order as final.
material_facts: A Revenue Officer rejected the landholder’s claim that a partition had taken place and determined that surplus land existed.
The appellate authority confirmed the Revenue Officer’s determination and dismissed the appeal.
The landholder sought revision from a higher authority, which refused to entertain it on the ground that the appellate order was final.
The dispute arose under the scheme before its amendment, and the statute authorized higher authorities to examine records and revise orders in proceedings under the Act.
issues.conclusion: The appellate order was capable of revision by the Collector under section 59 before the amendment. The appeal was dismissed, leaving in place the High Court’s ruling that revision was available.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 44(1) and 44(2) make the Revenue Officer’s order final subject to the result of an appeal, but that finality does not curtail the broad revisional powers in section 59(1) and (2) over orders and proceedings under the Act. The finality provision allows the consequences of the determination, including vesting and settlement of surplus land under section 45, to proceed if the aggrieved person takes no further step. Section 58’s separate appeal route does not create a conflict. The 1975 amendment specifying revision did not establish that revision had been unavailable under the earlier wording. The Court distinguished J. K. Cotton Spinning & Weaving Mills Co. Ltd. v. State of U.P. and applied the harmonious-construction principle discussed in The Bengal Immunity Company Ltd. v. The State of Bihar. Given the expropriatory nature of the Act and the initial determination by revenue authorities, the statutory scheme supported correction of errors or irregularities by higher authorities.

rule.if: original_scheme_applies and land_ceiling_case and revenue_officer_determined_surplus and appellate_authority_confirmed_determination and higher_authority_revision_power_covers_appellate_orders and finality_language_allows_further_steps

predicates.original_scheme_applies: The dispute arose under the statutory scheme before its amendment.
predicates.land_ceiling_case: The proceeding concerned the determination of surplus land under a land-ceiling scheme.
predicates.revenue_officer_determined_surplus: A revenue officer determined whether land held by a person exceeded the permitted ceiling.
predicates.appellate_authority_confirmed_determinat: An appellate authority confirmed the revenue officer’s determination.
predicates.higher_authority_revision_power_covers_a: The governing scheme authorized a higher authority to revise orders made on appeal by a lower-ranking officer.
predicates.finality_language_allows_further_steps: The governing scheme described the initial order as final subject to the appeal’s result, without expressly excluding further review.

issues.definition: When the original scheme applies to a land-ceiling case in which an appellate authority has confirmed a revenue officer’s surplus determination, and the scheme grants a higher authority broad power to revise appellate orders while its finality language does not exclude further review, the appellate order is revisable by that higher authority.
